claude.country: United States and United Kingdom/Canada (SEER and METABRIC cohorts)
claude.sample_unit: patients in the METABRIC external validation cohort (SEER training n = 4,024)

links.outcome: Calibration (ECE) of SEER-fit calibrators on external METABRIC cohort versus internal SEER test
links.effect: Isotonic regression reduced SEER test ECE by 50–92%, but the same calibrators applied unchanged to METABRIC increased ECE by a factor of two to three for every model.
links.quote: The same SEER-fit calibrators, applied unchanged to METABRIC, increased ECE by a factor of two to three for every model on both the imputed and complete-case external cohorts, a direct consequence of the base-rate shift from 84.7% to 42.1% alive.

links.outcome: Calibration miscalibration persistence after population base-rate shift
links.effect: Base-rate shift from 84.7% to 42.1% alive increased ECE two- to threefold; authors conclude predicted probabilities require per-cohort recalibration on a labeled target sample.
links.quote: feature-level explanations can be reported with confidence across cohorts, but predicted probabilities require per-cohort recalibration on a labeled sample of the target population.

links.outcome: Calibration suitability of a model to a different population without local recalibration
links.effect: SEER-fit calibrators increased ECE two- to threefold on METABRIC for all models; per-cohort recalibration recommended.
links.quote: Calibration and feature importance dissociate under prevalence shift: probability scale is cohort-specific, but feature ranking is cohort-stable.

Validating SHAP explanations via cross-validation stability, clinical-alignment scoring, and cross-model rank correlation

links.effect: SEER-fit calibrators increased ECE two- to three-fold on METABRIC; alive rate shifted from 84.7% to 42.1%.
links.quote: The same SEER-fit calibrators, applied unchanged to METABRIC, increased ECE by a factor of two to three for every model on both the imputed and complete-case external cohorts, a direct consequence of the base-rate shift from 84.7% to 42.1% alive.

links.effect: ECE increased by a factor of two to three for every model under base-rate shift from 84.7% to 42.1% alive.
links.quote: The same SEER-fit calibrators, applied unchanged to METABRIC, increased ECE by a factor of two to three for every model on both the imputed and complete-case external cohorts, a direct consequence of the base-rate shift from 84.7% to 42.1% alive.

links.effect: SEER-fit calibrators increased external ECE two- to three-fold for every model on imputed and complete-case METABRIC cohorts.
links.quote: The same SEER-fit calibrators, applied unchanged to METABRIC, increased ECE by a factor of two to three for every model on both the imputed and complete-case external cohorts, a direct consequence of the base-rate shift from 84.7% to 42.1% alive.

links.effect: Tree models: ρ ≈ 0.94 (p < 0.01); LR/MLP positive but non-significant (ρ = 0.66 and 0.71).
links.quote: By contrast, SHAP feature-importance rankings transferred strongly across cohorts in the five-model base-model analysis: tree-based models (RF, XGB, LGBM) achieved SEER–METABRIC Spearman rank correlations of ρ ≈ 0.94 (p < 0.01), with Age and Nodes Positive top-ranked in both cohorts; LR and MLP showed positive but non-significant agreement (ρ = 0.66 and 0.71, respectively) in the six-feature setting.
